cosmetology.hero.title2: The right ingredients make them work.
cosmetology.hero.description: In formulation development, what matters is not only the function of an individual ingredient, but also its effect on the overall system. That is why we approach ingredient selection in terms of application, specifications and practical needs. Developing a new formulation, qualifying a supplier or looking for an alternative? Explore ingredients worth evaluating and request a sample for your own testing.

cosmetology.challenges.title: The challenges formulators face
cosmetology.challenges.title1: One change affects the entire system
cosmetology.challenges.description1: Adding an ingredient for a specific function can change viscosity, foaming, stability or after-feel. Every modification therefore needs to be assessed in the context of the complete formulation, rather than a single parameter.
cosmetology.challenges.description2: A formula may pass stability tests yet still feel too heavy, tacky or difficult to apply. The challenge is to find the right balance between structure, stability and the desired sensory profile.
cosmetology.challenges.description3: The same INCI name does not always mean the same behaviour in a formulation. When reformulating, what matters is function, application performance and the effect of the change on the entire system, not just the ingredient name.
cosmetology.challenges.description4: Rather than testing numerous options at random, narrow the selection to a few ingredients chosen on the basis of function, specifications, documentation and availability. Each can then be evaluated in your own laboratory.
cosmetology.challenges.callout: Each of these challenges can arise in different types of formulations and at different stages of a project. Explore five areas where ingredient selection is particularly important.
cosmetology.guide.description: Different formulation objectives call for different ingredient selection criteria. Choose one of the five areas below to explore the functions, specifications and ingredients to consider for further testing.
cosmetology.guide.tip: The choice of ingredient and its use level must always be verified in the specific formulation, based on technical documentation and application testing.
cosmetology.process.title: From formulation needs to a sample in your lab
cosmetology.process.step1.title: Formulation objective
cosmetology.process.step1.description: We start with the function, desired result or constraint that matters to your project. This helps us identify the ingredient properties that are truly relevant.
cosmetology.process.step2.title: Selection criteria
cosmetology.process.step2.description: We assess the ingredient's function, application properties and project requirements to narrow the search.
cosmetology.process.step2.highlight: We start with what the formulation needs, rather than with a catalogue.
cosmetology.process.step3.title: Ingredient selection
cosmetology.process.step3.description: We identify ingredients to consider first, together with the key technical and application information.
cosmetology.process.step3.highlight: Instead of numerous options chosen at random, you receive a few carefully considered options for further evaluation.
cosmetology.process.step4.title: Laboratory evaluation
cosmetology.process.step4.description: We provide documentation and samples of selected ingredients for testing in your own formulation. The results help confirm the selection or guide the next iteration.
cosmetology.process.callout: We do not start with a product list. We start with what your formulation needs.
